_doc: Family split template (lexeme_aligner.split_gen --family). Slots give the ORDER and what each slot may render; the forms are learned per language from its own text and word alignment (grounding: an affix is kept only where its words link to one of the slot's features). Prefix slots are counted from the word start, suffix slots from the stem outward. `one_letter`: a one-letter form may fill the slot. `renders`: feature prefixes (neg, pn=, person=, tense=, mood=, voice=, fn=<lemma>, obj, case=, plural). Nouns are not cut: noun class prefixes are agreement, and cutting them lost link stability on Zinza (2026-11-28). Reference: make-tanakh's Zinza bundle zin/d33c99ab (ni-/ti-/ku- 1, subject 2, a-/ka- 3, object 4; -il 1, -w 2, -a/-e/-ile 3). With `vote`: slots are filled by lexeme_aligner.split_vote (paradigm vote after make-tanakh-research's Swahili analyser); `seeds` = Swahili's closed lists (make-tanakh-research lab/training/grammar/swh.json (MIT), closed lists from Ashton 1944 / Mohammed 2001), starting forms only, each still grounded per language. Settings measured 2026-11-28 (internal-docs/split-generator-plan-2026-11-28.md): seeds only (text_forms false), final vowel cut by the vote alone (ground false).
seeds_credit: make-tanakh-research lab/training/grammar/swh.json (MIT), closed lists from Ashton 1944 / Mohammed 2001; plus common Proto-Bantu concords and tense/negative forms (after Meeussen 1967, Bantu Grammatical Reconstructions)
